subject: AIPAC explained
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

We just launched a coalition of 20+ progressive groups united to demand
the Democratic Party reject AIPAC, but you might be wondering, who is
AIPAC anyway?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20240312._4NgUG&refcode=em20240312-33767&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=3&t=1001&akid=33767%2E1203867%2EnTeLkh ]If you already know the deal about AIPAC and want to fuel our work to
stop their dangerous influence in Washington, chip in here.

Otherwise, here’s an explainer on AIPAC and why we’re taking them on:

AIPAC stands for the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, a lobby
group founded in the 1950s to build bipartisan support for Israel in
Congress.

For most of AIPAC’s existence, it didn’t get involved in elections. They
didn’t need to. But following the groundbreaking elections of AOC, Rashida
Tlaib, Ilhan Omar, and Ayanna Pressley, Congress for the first time had
members willing to speak out for Palestinian human rights. The Democratic
base began to shift on the issue, recognizing Israel’s apartheid rule over
Palestinians.

As a result, in 2021 AIPAC formed its own PAC and Super PAC known as
United Democracy Project (UDP) that waded into Democratic primaries,
spending millions against progressive, pro-peace candidates like Summer
Lee and Ilhan Omar.

Let’s be clear: AIPAC’s campaign spending is a sign of weakness.
Unconditional support for Israel’s far-right government has been
significantly weakened, particularly among Democratic voters. AIPAC’s
tactic of last resort is to threaten to spend millions of dollars to
silence anyone who may speak out for Palestinian human rights.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20240312._4NgUG&refcode=em20240312-33767&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=3&t=1002&akid=33767%2E1203867%2EnTeLkh ]That’s why it’s so important that we have the Squad’s back. We can’t
let AIPAC’s fear tactics work. Chip in now to help us reject AIPAC and
re-elect the Squad in 2024.

So where does AIPAC’s funding come from? While they claim to be
bipartisan, AIPAC is fueled by massive donations from millionaires and
billionaires, including right-wing megadonors who’ve donated to Donald
Trump, Ron DeSantis, and Nikki Haley. The same people trying to re-elect
Trump are bankrolling AIPAC’s primaries against the Squad.

AIPAC’s dark money influence is widespread: last cycle, only 33 out of 535
members of Congress did not receive money from the group's network. Who
AIPAC targets, however, is a narrow group of candidates and elected
officials. AIPAC’s Super PAC exclusively spends against Democrats in
primaries — particularly young, Black and brown progressive champions like
the Squad. In fact, more than 85% of the money UDP (AIPAC’s Super PAC) has
spent has been against candidates of color.

Not only that, but AIPAC has ardently endorsed and contributed to 109
Republican insurrectionists who denied the 2020 election results, as well
as more than 200 anti-abortion Republican extremists. They recently
congratulated retiring Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell on a job
well done for his decades of work stonewalling progress, stacking the
SCOTUS with Republicans, and pushing a far-right agenda.

All in all, AIPAC is a right-wing organization, and it’s our job to build
a movement to expose their right-wing agenda to all voters so that they
are rejected by the Democratic Party, following the same path as other
lobby groups like the NRA.

That fight starts now. AIPAC and its affiliates are going all-out to try
and take down the Squad and any other Democrat who expresses support for a
ceasefire and peace in Gaza. Last year, they announced plans to spend an
unprecedented $100 million in this year’s elections. They’ve already run
attack ads against Jamaal Bowman, Summer Lee, and Cori Bush while
hand-picking their primary opponents.

Enough is enough. It is time for the Democratic Party as a whole to do
what’s right and stand up against AIPAC’s threat to our democracy.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20240312._4NgUG&refcode=em20240312-33767&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=3&t=1003&akid=33767%2E1203867%2EnTeLkh ]We’re fighting back against AIPAC’s attacks on the Squad while pushing
for ALL Democratic candidates to reject their dark money once and for all:
will you pitch in $3 or whatever you can to support our
Reject AIPAC campaign?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20240312._4NgUG&refcode=em20240312-33767&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=3&t=1022&akid=33767%2E1203867%2EnTeLkh ]Contribute $3

We’ve defeated AIPAC and its millions of dollars of right-wing megadonor
money before — now more than ever, we need to do it again, and we need to
put an end to their interference in our Democratic elections.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

body:
Pramila knows what is at stake and is fighting for progress in Congress every day.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20240312-3622-footer&t=1&akid=3622%2E420207%2ENm0UiK)
Did you catch Pramila’s op-ed in Popsugar, Peter?
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/48116?source=em20240312-3622&t=2&akid=3622%2E420207%2ENm0UiK)

| | **Today is Equal Pay Day, a day that serves as a reminder of the persistent gender pay gap in the United States.** March 12, represents how far into the following year the average woman would need to work to earn the same amount of money her male counterparts work in the same role. That date goes even deeper into the calendar year for women of color. On average, Black women earn only 63 cents, Indigenous women only 57 cents, and Hispanic women just 55 cents for every dollar earned by white men. **This intersectionality compounds the economic disparities faced by marginalized communities, exacerbating systemic inequities.** Pay inequality is perpetuated by various factors, including gender bias in hiring and promotion, occupational segregation, and lack of transparency in salary negotiations. Women, on average, earn just 82 cents for every dollar earned by men, with the gap even wider for certain groups. **The solution is simple: equal pay for equal work.** How do we get there? By raising awareness, advocating for policies like pay transparency and anti-discrimination measures, and supporting initiatives that promote equal pay, and hold employers accountable to ensure fair compensation — regardless of gender identity. **In Congress, I have cosponsored several pieces of legislation seeking to establish equal pay for equal work, including legislation that would:**
* Raise the federal minimum wage to $15 per hour and tie future increases to the median hourly wage;
* Ensure people are paid based on their skills and experience, not their gender;
* Allow lower-wage workers to request for flexibility of their schedules without retaliation; and
* Help end discrimination against pregnant women and parents in the workplace.

Together, we can create a more equitable future for all. _Rick_ | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution instantly:

| $10, one time.

That is the donation we are asking you to make to Elissa Slotkin's campaign for Senate in Michigan and the Voter Protection Project today.

Yesterday, Donald Trump endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers in our Senate race. We'll look back at this moment as a major inflection point in our race, and one where Elissa needs your help if we're going to win.

[_If that's all you need to hear, use this link to donate directly to Elissa Slotkin's campaign today »_](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/64177?t=6&akid=13420%2E878179%2EJTRNrw)

$10 because Trump's endorsement is an acknowledgement of how important Michigan is to his success -- something we've always known about the importance of the state to Democrats' chances of holding the Senate and White House.

$10 because now that Trump is paying attention to this race, the attacks against Elissa are sure to ramp up and we'll need your help to fight back.

It’s ironic, because Mike Rogers criticized Donald Trump for a long time. He criticized him on CNN for years and called him “more gangster than presidential.” Today, without shame, he eagerly accepted his endorsement. He did it because he'll do anything to get elected and he won't stop there.

Mike Rogers has Trump. Elissa has you. And if lots and lots of people donate to her campaign today, we'll be well on our way toward securing the resources we need to win this race.

body:
Missouri is on the frontlines of the fight for power in our country.
#
Peter,
I’m running for U.S. Senate because I want everyday Missourians to call the shots in our country — not giant corporations or the cowards like Josh Hawley they’ve bought off in Washington. **This email is long, but I hope you’ll take some time to read it:**
**[CHIP IN NOW →](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/44493?refcode=em20240312-5016&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=5016%2E614464%2EWAGdVj)**
**When I came home between deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan, it was clear to me that Missouri is on the frontlines of the fight for power in our country.**
While communities like mine all across our state were stripped for parts, corrupt politicians like Josh Hawley attacked workers with anti-union schemes like “Right-to-Work” and fought to block wage increases for Missouri families — all to enrich multinational corporations and mega-donors who bankroll their campaigns and their careers.
They helped Wall Street financiers sell off our farmland to billionaires in China and Brazil — devastating rural communities and contributing to the closure of 90% of Missouri hog producers in a single generation.
One of Missouri’s oldest and largest employers, Anheuser-Busch, was sold to a Belgian conglomerate — costing Missouri more than a thousand jobs.
Missouri-based Monsanto, one of the world’s most important agrochemical and biotechnology companies, was sold to Germany — eliminating even more jobs.
And as dozens more headquarters have been taken out of state, politicians in power like Josh Hawley were happy to sit back and watch it happen.
**Manufacturing, agriculture, production — they’re shipping it all away to foreign oligarchs who don’t care about working people in our state.** And while our communities were getting gutted, these same politicians voted time and time again to spend trillions of dollars and thousands of lives on overseas wars that got their Big Oil friends rich.
These politicians have spent decades sparking phony culture wars to distract and divide our families. They’ve become so obsessed with controlling our lives, they made Missouri the first state in the nation to ban abortion — without exceptions for victims of rape or incest.
**Our state deserves a Senator who will stand up and fight for it — and I’m ready to serve.[So if you’re ready to elect a real warrior for working people to Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat, will you please rush a donation of any amount toward my grassroots campaign today?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/44493?refcode=em20240312-5016&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=5016%2E614464%2EWAGdVj)**

[Contribute $10](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/44494?refcode=em20240312-5016&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=10&t=3&akid=5016%2E614464%2EWAGdVj) [Contribute $25](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/44494?refcode=em20240312-5016&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=25&t=4&akid=5016%2E614464%2EWAGdVj) [Give another amount](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/44493?refcode=em20240312-5016&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=5016%2E614464%2EWAGdVj)
---
We aren’t fighting the corporate status quo just to make a point, either. **This is a race we really can win.**
Our values have won at the ballot box in Missouri for referendums that go beyond what’s happening nowadays in Washington, or even what political elites in Jefferson City are willing to allow.
For the last three election cycles, Missouri voters have side-stepped our politicians by voting to increase the minimum wage well above the federal level, expand health care, repeal an anti-worker “Right-to-Work” scheme, legalize weed, and enact more protections against political corruption with wide margins.
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/44493?refcode=em20240312-5016&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=6&akid=5016%2E614464%2EWAGdVj)
**So now, we’re building a record-breaking, people-powered movement to defeat Josh Hawley and take this Senate seat back for working Missourians.**
Together, we’re going to stop printing money for Wall Street and start funding our schools enough to get Missouri out of last place for starting teacher pay.
We’re going to abolish corporate PACs and demand a government that safeguards our democracy and holds corrupt politicians accountable.
We’re going to take back Missouri farmland for Missouri farmers and start manufacturing essential drugs right here in America.
We’re going to build an economy that puts American workers and small businesses in charge, not giant corporations and foreign oligarchs — an economy that invests in putting America first in the next generation of energy, semiconductors, and supply chain independence.
We’re going to put an end to pointless, trillion-dollar wars and invest in a Marshall Plan for the Midwest — a historic investment in our workers and communities to rebuild our forgotten towns and cities, and to finally start making stuff in America again.
And we’re going to finally put everyday Missourians in charge of their own neighborhoods, workplaces, and bodies.
**It’s time to take our power back — and we can’t do it without your support.[So please, will you rush a donation of absolutely any amount to my campaign today? I’m not taking a cent from corporate PACs in this race so you’ll always know I’m fighting for everyday, working people in the U.S. Senate.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/44493?refcode=em20240312-5016&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=7&akid=5016%2E614464%2EWAGdVj)**

clean_body: | | | President Biden’s 2025 federal budget proposal is a progressive blueprint that prioritizes the economic well-being of middle and lower-income families as well as create a more equitable, sustainable, and prosperous future for all Americans. The budget prioritizes healthcare expansion through Medicare improvements and lower prescription costs, while investing in education. It tackles climate change through clean energy initiatives fostering green jobs and economic growth while leveling the playing field for all. Funding for these initiatives will come from increased taxes on the wealthiest individuals and corporations, promoting inclusive and sustainable economic growth. Derek Marshall has felt the sting of a broken system, living paycheck to paycheck. Now he is fighting for justice, equality, and progressive issues like Medicare for All and a Green New Deal to improve the lives of the people of California. While Republicans continue to be vague about who and how their budget proposal will impact Americans, Biden’s proposal is transparent, detailing how he would correct the inequities created by Trump and the Republicans’ tax cuts. The majority of the budget would cover programs like Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security, and veterans’ benefits. Another key theme in the plan is helping families afford their basic needs, from mortgage assistance, student loan assistance, and affordable child care. These things are all possible when the wealthy pay their fair share. **** ****Thanks for your support. -Derek Marshall for Congress is a Democrat running for Congress in California's 23rd District. Thank you. Our first ad is on the air.
#

Thanks to the support of people like you, our first television ad of the campaign went up today. I’m very proud of the ad -- it talks about my life in the Marines, my family, and my time in Congress.
[**Please watch the ad and make a $3 contribution to help keep us on the air.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ruben-em-ad24?noskip=true&refcode=em240312-2-160&refcode2=2067_734936_pFM-v6&akid=2067%2E734936%2EpFM-v6)

Peter -
Never in a million years would I have thought that winning Arizona’s Senate seat, holding our majority in the Senate and saving our democracy itself would fall to me.
Growing up the way I did, that would’ve been unthinkable.
And even now, after serving in Iraq as a Marine, after several years in Congress, after living through an insurrection at the Capitol... it’s hard for me to believe.
But here we are – in the heat of a political campaign that will determine control of the Senate.
Today, we went up on the air with our first ad. Going up first gives us a tremendous advantage and it’s not something that would have been possible without the support of hundreds of thousands of people who have contributed to my campaign for Senate.
That’s something else I could have never imagined.
I’m very proud of the ad. I hope you’ll watch it. It’d mean a lot to me, especially because it wouldn’t have been possible without supporters like you.
I hope the ad makes you proud to be a part of this campaign as well.
[**Please watch our first ad and make a contribution of $3 (or more if you can) to help keep us on the air. Your support would mean a lot to me today.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ruben-em-ad24?noskip=true&refcode=em240312-2-160&refcode2=2067_734936_pFM-v6&akid=2067%2E734936%2EpFM-v6)

name: Wes Moore
subject: With Trump as the presumptive GOP nominee, Democratic governors are more important than ever
body:
Friend,

When I ran for Governor in 2022, the Democratic Governors Association (DGA) was on my side. Our historic victory wouldn’t have been possible without their support.

Now, as we head into another critical election year, the DGA is working around the clock to secure more Democratic victories in 2024.
The stakes couldn’t be higher. With Trump as the presumptive GOP nominee for president, Democratic governors will be more important than ever. Much like Trump, GOP extremists are running for governorships across the country with the promise to roll back critical rights. From North Carolina to Texas to California, democratic governors serve as the last line of defense against the MAGA agenda and GOP attacks on our freedoms.
Our most fundamental rights are on the line this election. We cannot lose the progress Democratic governors, like me, are making across the country to protect our democracy and enshrine reproductive rights. By building strong coalitions now, we can win battleground states and increase the number of Democratic governors across the country.

So friend, will you help support the groundwork the DGA is doing now to protect Democratic incumbents and elect more Democratic governors in 2024? As the only organization dedicated to electing Democratic governors nationwide, the DGA is relying on grassroots supporters just like you. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240312-1?refcode=em20240312]

Support the DGA » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240312-1?refcode=em20240312]

Thank you for supporting this critical work.

Elevate,
Wes Moore

name: John Avlon
subject: There's no debate.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOHN AVLON FOR CONGRESS
body:
Friends,

Campaigns come down to contrasts, and last night's debate made that even clearer.

That's what we learned from last night's candidate forum in East Hampton -- and that applies not just to the primary, but to the general election. Long Island families need someone in Congress who's able to get past the hyper-partisanship that has crippled Congress and actually get to work.

To beat whichever of the two faces of Trumpism wins the GOP primary election -- and yes, you probably saw George Santos is challenging Nick LaLota -- we need to win over Independents and even some Republicans who can't stomach the MAGA chaos. We can do this -- by coming together and showing that our country and community is not as divided or dysfunctional as Donald Trump would have you believe.

There's no debate about this: We have to build the broadest possible coalition to win back this seat from Trump's MAGA minions this fall. Please make a contribution today and help us keep growing our movement. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avlon-donate-debate?refcode=em0312]

Here is the contrast in this election: Dysfunction and hyper-partisanship on one side -- or reviving the promise of our democracy, making government work again, and common sense problem solving on the other. If we don't win back the House, we can't defend women's reproductive freedoms, strengthen the middle class, invest in transportation and infrastructure, and take on climate change. We'll be stuck in an even deeper rut of MAGA-led dysfunction.

As I've been talking to families across Suffolk County -- I understand folks' frustration when politicians don't deliver on what we sent them to Congress to do. We're seeing that now with Nick LaLota putting Trump's interests ahead of ours. We need more courage and common sense from our elected representatives. We need less fighting and more fixing.

You've heard me say it before: This election is not a drill. And last night proved why. If you're with me, please support my campaign today: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avlon-donate-debate?refcode=em0312b]

Donate $10 today >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avlon-donate-debate?refcode=em0312c&amount=10]

Donate $100 today >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avlon-donate-debate?refcode=em0312c&amount=100]

Thank you for fighting the good fight with me.

-John

body:
Peter, this is our campaign’s biggest moment yet. | | |
---
Peter -- Just a few minutes ago, _this team helped me clinch the Democratic Party’s nomination for President of the United States._ It’ll all be official come the Party’s convention in August, but before then, let me say this: **_Thank you._** Millions of voters across the country have made their voices heard in these early primaries, and I could not be more grateful for your support. Truly. It means the world to me. **Whether you’ve had a chance to vote for me and Kamala, chip in a few bucks to our campaign, or even share our message with folks in your community: You’re showing that you’re ready to fight back against Donald Trump’s extreme plans to take us backwards.** _This election is a choice between those who want to pull America back to the past, and those who want to move America into the future. So when I say your support matters, I really mean it._ _In 2020, 74,223,369 people voted for Donald Trump. However, 81,282,916 voted for Kamala and me. So I do not need to tell you how slim the margin of victory is and how much of an impact you have._ Kamala and I are relying on you to step up for the first time today so that we can continue to move America forward. [Please, donate to LCV Victory Fund today to help defeat Trump and other pro-polluter candidates. Your contribution will be tripled if you give today >>](https://links.messages.lcv.)

Our electoral campaigns have a proven track record of turning the tide when and where it matters most. **In 2020, when we spoke with voters about Trump 's climate-killing policies, their votes shifted in a serious way** -- as much as a 20-point swing in some places -- and helped deliver battleground states to Biden.

We have proof that these early conversations to persuade voters really change minds. But we don't stop there. When it comes to voter turnout, our organizers help educate voters on the process of requesting and returning vote-by-mail ballots. They help voters make a voting plan by giving them precinct-specific information. For voters who vote by mail, our organizers follow up by mail, phone, and again at their doors to make sure their ballots are submitted and counted on time.

We aim to make three passes on each voter's door on our list. And the strategy _works_.

I promise you, your contribution will have a real and direct impact on the outcome of key races -- and the future of our planet.

[The most effective thing you can do to win critical races for the environment is to donate to LCV Victory Fund. Every contribution before the end of the month will be tripled, so please don't wait >>](https://links.messages.lcv.)
